items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So we hired Lude officially... Lude would relieve us.

ctx.x: ...there was a young trombone player from the British West Indies named Herman Wilson, who had not been very long in Paris and I made his acquaintance with a friend of his named Donald Brown. I was in need of some musicians for my coming jobs in Zurich at the Hungaria -Esquire in June and August in Blankenberge. Donald played bongos and Congo drums, but had never played jazz drums in an orchestra. However, he said that he had a little experience on drums and thought he would catch on to the technique of playing…

The rehearsals went along very well, and Benny made some arrangements to add to those that I had in the books. Everything was cool until the day before we were to leave for Zurich,which was the 30th. A fellow who was also from Martinique came to our hotel and introduced himself, and said that he was a replacement for the bass player. This man's name was Lude. I had seen him around Pigalle, where most of the musicians met, but did not know that he was a bass player until this meeting. Lily and I thought that this…

So we decided to go see this cat and find out what his story was. I was upset because he had made all the rehearsals with the band, and the working permits were given individually, so one was at his name. He was also on the photos of the orchestra, that I had a photographer to take, and now he was sending someone else to take his place!
